verses.1: The Israelites acted treacherously in regard to the devoted things, and Achan son of Karmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah from the tribe of Judah, took from the devoted things. The anger of the LORD burned against the Israelites.
verses.2: Joshua sent men from Jericho to the village of Ai, which is near Bethel, and said to them, “Go up and scout the land.” The men went up and scouted Ai.
verses.3: They returned to Joshua and said, “Do not let the whole people go up, but let about three thousand men go up and strike Ai. Do not bring the whole people there, for it is a small place.”
verses.4: So about three thousand men went up from the people, but they were routed before the men of Ai.
verses.5: The men of Ai struck them, killing about thirty-six of them, and chased them before the gate as far as the ravines, beating them down, and the people’s hearts turned to water.
verses.6: Joshua tore his clothes and fell on his face to the ground before the ark of the LORD until evening, he and the elders of Israel, and they put dust on their heads.
verses.7: Joshua said, “Alas, O Lord YHWH, why have you brought this people across the Jordan to deliver us into the hands of the Amorites to destroy us? If only we had been content to dwell beyond the Jordan!”
verses.8: What will you say? After Israel has turned its back before its enemies!
verses.9: And when the Canaanites and all the inhabitants of the land hear of this, they will surround us and cut us off from the land, and what will you do for your great name?”
verses.10: The LORD said to Joshua, “Get up! Why are you lying face down on the ground?
verses.11: Israel has sinned and has broken my covenant that I commanded them. They have taken from the devoted things, and they have stolen and lied and hidden them among their possessions.
verses.12: So the Israelites cannot stand before their enemies. They will turn their backs before their enemies, for they have become devoted. I will no longer be with you, unless you destroy the devoted things from among you.
verses.13: Get up, consecrate the people and say, ‘Consecrate yourselves tomorrow, for this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: A devoted thing is among you, Israel. You cannot stand before your enemies until you remove the devoted thing from among you.’”
verses.14: In the morning you will come near by your tribes, and the tribe that the LORD shows to be the one will come near by its families, and the family that the LORD shows to be the one will come near by its households, and the household that the LORD shows to be the one will come near by the individuals.
verses.15: The one who is found to be the one who took the devoted thing will be burned with fire, he and all that belongs to him, for he has broken my covenant and has done a disgraceful thing in Israel.”
verses.16: Joshua rose early in the morning and brought Israel near by their tribes, and the tribe of Judah was selected.
verses.17: He brought the families of Judah near, and the family of Zerah was selected. He brought the family of Zerah near by its households, and the household of Zabdi was selected.
verses.18: He brought the household of Zabdi near by the individuals, and Achan son of Karmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah from the tribe of Judah, was selected.
verses.19: Joshua said to Achan, “My son, give glory to the LORD, the God of Israel, and make confession to him. Now tell me what you have done. Do not hide it from me.”
verses.20: Achan answered Joshua, “Truly, I have sinned to the LORD, the God of Israel. This is what I did.”
verses.21: “I saw among the spoil a beautiful robe from Shinar, two hundred shekels of silver, and a bar of gold weighing fifty shekels. I coveted them and took them, and here they are, hidden in my tent, with the silver beneath them.”
verses.22: Joshua sent messengers, and they ran to the tent, and there they found the things hidden in the tent, with the silver beneath them.
verses.23: They took them out from the tent and brought them to Joshua and to all the Israelites, and they set them before the LORD.
verses.24: Joshua took Achan, son of Zerah, and the silver, and the robe, and the bar of gold, and his sons and daughters, and his ox, and his donkey, and his sheep, and all that belonged to him, and all the Israelites with him, and brought them up to the Valley of Achor.
verses.25: Joshua said, “What have you brought trouble to us? The LORD will bring trouble to you today.” Then all Israel stoned him, and they burned them with fire, and they struck them with stones.
verses.26: They built a large pile of stones over him, which remains to this day. Therefore the place was named the Valley of Achor.

notes:
Notes
- v. 1: “acted treacherously” translates מַעַל, which carries connotations of betrayal or deceit.
- v. 21: “a bar of gold weighing fifty shekels” is based on the Hebrew text, which refers to a single bar, not individual pieces.
- v. 24: “Valley of Achor” follows the Hebrew term עֵמֶק עָכוֹר, which is the etymology for the name given in the Septuagint as Emekachor. The notes in the Septuagint mention Emekachor but the Hebrew term is retained here as Valley of Achor.
- v. 25: “What have you brought trouble to us?” reflects the Hebrew phrase מֶה עֲכַרְתָּנוּ, which is a rhetorical question expressing frustration.
raw:
[1] The Israelites acted treacherously in regard to the devoted things, and Achan son of Karmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah from the tribe of Judah, took from the devoted things. The anger of the LORD burned against the Israelites.

[2] Joshua sent men from Jericho to the village of Ai, which is near Bethel, and said to them, “Go up and scout the land.” The men went up and scouted Ai.

[3] They returned to Joshua and said, “Do not let the whole people go up, but let about three thousand men go up and strike Ai. Do not bring the whole people there, for it is a small place.”

[4] So about three thousand men went up from the people, but they were routed before the men of Ai.

[5] The men of Ai struck them, killing about thirty-six of them, and chased them before the gate as far as the ravines, beating them down, and the people’s hearts turned to water.

[6] Joshua tore his clothes and fell on his face to the ground before the ark of the LORD until evening, he and the elders of Israel, and they put dust on their heads.

[7] Joshua said, “Alas, O Lord YHWH, why have you brought this people across the Jordan to deliver us into the hands of the Amorites to destroy us? If only we had been content to dwell beyond the Jordan!”

[8] What will you say? After Israel has turned its back before its enemies!

[9] And when the Canaanites and all the inhabitants of the land hear of this, they will surround us and cut us off from the land, and what will you do for your great name?”

[10] The LORD said to Joshua, “Get up! Why are you lying face down on the ground?

[11] Israel has sinned and has broken my covenant that I commanded them. They have taken from the devoted things, and they have stolen and lied and hidden them among their possessions.

[12] So the Israelites cannot stand before their enemies. They will turn their backs before their enemies, for they have become devoted. I will no longer be with you, unless you destroy the devoted things from among you.

[13] Get up, consecrate the people and say, ‘Consecrate yourselves tomorrow, for this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: A devoted thing is among you, Israel. You cannot stand before your enemies until you remove the devoted thing from among you.’”

[14] In the morning you will come near by your tribes, and the tribe that the LORD shows to be the one will come near by its families, and the family that the LORD shows to be the one will come near by its households, and the household that the LORD shows to be the one will come near by the individuals.

[15] The one who is found to be the one who took the devoted thing will be burned with fire, he and all that belongs to him, for he has broken my covenant and has done a disgraceful thing in Israel.”

[16] Joshua rose early in the morning and brought Israel near by their tribes, and the tribe of Judah was selected.

[17] He brought the families of Judah near, and the family of Zerah was selected. He brought the family of Zerah near by its households, and the household of Zabdi was selected.

[18] He brought the household of Zabdi near by the individuals, and Achan son of Karmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah from the tribe of Judah, was selected.

[19] Joshua said to Achan, “My son, give glory to the LORD, the God of Israel, and make confession to him. Now tell me what you have done. Do not hide it from me.”

[20] Achan answered Joshua, “Truly, I have sinned to the LORD, the God of Israel. This is what I did.”

[21] “I saw among the spoil a beautiful robe from Shinar, two hundred shekels of silver, and a bar of gold weighing fifty shekels. I coveted them and took them, and here they are, hidden in my tent, with the silver beneath them.”

[22] Joshua sent messengers, and they ran to the tent, and there they found the things hidden in the tent, with the silver beneath them.

[23] They took them out from the tent and brought them to Joshua and to all the Israelites, and they set them before the LORD.

[24] Joshua took Achan, son of Zerah, and the silver, and the robe, and the bar of gold, and his sons and daughters, and his ox, and his donkey, and his sheep, and all that belonged to him, and all the Israelites with him, and brought them up to the Valley of Achor.

[25] Joshua said, “What have you brought trouble to us? The LORD will bring trouble to you today.” Then all Israel stoned him, and they burned them with fire, and they struck them with stones.

[26] They built a large pile of stones over him, which remains to this day. Therefore the place was named the Valley of Achor.

Notes
- v. 1: “acted treacherously” translates מַעַל, which carries connotations of betrayal or deceit.
- v. 21: “a bar of gold weighing fifty shekels” is based on the Hebrew text, which refers to a single bar, not individual pieces.
- v. 24: “Valley of Achor” follows the Hebrew term עֵמֶק עָכוֹר, which is the etymology for the name given in the Septuagint as Emekachor. The notes in the Septuagint mention Emekachor but the Hebrew term is retained here as Valley of Achor.
- v. 25: “What have you brought trouble to us?” reflects the Hebrew phrase מֶה עֲכַרְתָּנוּ, which is a rhetorical question expressing frustration.
